!!Public good alert!! 🚨🚨

Introducing Lory-4B and Lory-27B v1 🦜🦜, the first open-source decision models post-trained specifically to make simulated survey respondents follow economic logic. Off-the-shelf decision models can follow personas well but barely react to money at stake.

A fine-tune of Kev-4B and Kev-27B. Lory-27B performs on par with GPT-6.1-terra (no reasoning) at 1/5–1/10 of the price. Lory-4B is small enough to run on a 16 GB laptop at ~free cost.

They work best with EDSL (@ExpectedParrot's survey language). They're trained on its prompt format and ship with an adapter that runs any EDSL survey. And they respond to what's actually at stake: change the price, the odds or the payoff and the answer moves, not just the persona. One forward pass gives a full probability for every option.

This is just v1 of these models. I plan to continue post-training to make them the best decision models for simulated personas at the cheapest possible price.

note_tweet.text:
Global imbalances are back, and the conventional diagnosis may be wrong.

Conventional analysis by the International Monetary Fund, G7 + OECD traces the imbalances to domestic saving–investment gaps, pointing to "excess saving in China and the EU, and too little saving in the United States."

In a new working paper, GDP Center Non-Resident Senior Fellow @YanLian31677392  + Center Director @KevinPGallagher argue that the root cause of the imbalances is in fact the financial imbalances generated by the international monetary and financial system (IMFS) itself. Dollar dominance and the lack of a credible global lender of last resort push countries to self-insure.

For this month's T20 Summit in New York, the authors contribute to a policy brief ahead of the December G20 Leaders' Summit. They present two priorities for G20 discussions on imbalances:

📍 Strengthening the global financial safety net (GFSN)
📍 Accelerating multilateral development bank (MDB) reform

The goal is to make these systems "not just bigger, but better."

📄 Read the working paper: https://t.co/pcGGPECG2R
📄 Read the T20 policy brief: https://t.co/PonN5ZqftG
